At CesiumAstro, we are developers and pioneers of out-of-the-box communication systems for satellites, UAVs, launch vehicles, and other space and airborne platforms. We take pride in our dynamic and cross-functional work environment, which allows us to learn, develop, and engage across our organization. If you are looking for hands-on, interactive, and autonomous work, CesiumAstro is the place for you. We are actively seeking passionate, collaborative, energetic, and forward-thinking individuals to join our team. We are looking to add a Corporate Controller to our team. In this role you will oversee the accounting function responsible for general ledger accounting, financial close, reconciliations, and accounting compliance. This role establishes functional priorities and operating plans, manages accounting teams through subordinate leaders, and maintains accounting policies and controls that support accurate and timely financial reporting. The Corporate Controller evaluates financial results, complex accounting matters, internal controls, and operational performance to ensure accounting activities comply with applicable standards and organizational requirements. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, technically strong accounting leader with experience in complex multi entity environment and exposure to SEC reporting and SOX controls. This position requires an experienced accounting leader with deep knowledge of financial reporting, generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), internal controls, and audit requirements. The Corporate Controller partners cross-functionally with finance, operations, program management, and other business functions to address financial matters, improve accounting processes, and provide senior leadership with accurate and meaningful financial information. JOB DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Oversee accounting teams and subordinate leaders responsible for general ledger accounting, journal entries, account reconciliations, financial reporting, and related accounting activities. Establish functional priorities, operating plans, resource requirements, and performance expectations that support accurate and timely accounting operations. Develop accounting leaders and organizational capability through workforce planning, succession planning, performance management, and employee development. Provide SVP of accounting oversight of the organization's books and records, partnering with the senior finance leadership on corporate accounting strategy, technical accounting positions, and the integrity of financial data. Develop reporting packages for executive leadership and external stakeholders Lead process improvements, automation initiatives, and system enhancements Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual close activities, including journal entries, account reconciliations, accruals, adjustments, and financial statement preparation. Review financial results, balance sheet accounts, income statement activity, and supporting schedules to identify significant variances, discrepancies, or accounting issues. Present financial results, accounting matters, and reporting considerations to senior leadership to support informed business decisions. Own consolidated corporate financial reporting, including consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and the preparation of financial statements, disclosures, and management reporting packages. Establish and enforce accounting policies, procedures, internal controls, and documentation practices consistent with GAAP or IFRS and organizational requirements. Evaluate complex or non-routine accounting matters and determine appropriate accounting treatment, documentation, and financial reporting implications. Manage internal and external audit activities, including audit preparation, supporting documentation, issue resolution, and implementation of corrective actions. Ensure corporate compliance with applicable statutory, regulatory, and SEC reporting requirements and internal control over financial reporting (e.g., SOX), coordinating with tax, treasury, and external auditors. JOB REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, business administration, or a related field with 11-15 years of related experience, Master's degree with 9-12 years of related experience, or PhD with 7-10 years of related experience in accounting, financial reporting, audit, accounts payable, internal controls, or a related discipline. 5+ years of leadership or management experience leading finance, accounting, tax, internal controls, or business systems professionals. Active CPA License obtained within 18 months of starting. Experience serving in a corporate controller capacity or equivalent, including consolidated financial reporting, books-and-records integrity, technical accounting, and internal control over financial reporting. Expert knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting, general ledger accounting, financial close, and account reconciliation practices. Expertise in generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) or International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), accounting policies, and financial statement preparation. Comprehensive knowledge of internal controls, audit requirements, financial documentation, account analysis, and accounting compliance. Extensive experience evaluating complex accounting transactions, financial results, balance sheet activity, reporting issues, and appropriate accounting treatment. Strategic understanding of accounting operations, financial systems, process automation, control environments, and organizational reporting requirements. Exercises sound judgment in evaluating accounting issues, financial reporting implications, internal control risks, audit matters, and competing organizational priorities. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite including Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Teams. Enterprise resource planning (ERP), general ledger, and financial accounting applications, e.g. SAP, Oracle, , or equivalent applications. Financial close, account reconciliation, and consolidation applications used to support corporate controller responsibilities, e.g. FloQast, OneStream, or equivalent applications. Financial reporting, business intelligence, build Agents for work and processing automation and data analysis applications, e.g. Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent applications. This is an in-person internship located in our Austin, TX office. In this position, you will gain real-world experience and exposure to the finance and accounting professions in a hyper-growth start-up company by supporting many departments and helping carry out business transactions and projects. You will have the opportunity to work alongside senior staff and management personnel, developing technical skills and building professional relationships. Support various cross-department and cross-function projects impacting accounting and financial reporting, by working closely with different departments, including Supply Chain, Operations, Manufacturing, and Business Development. Get exposure to developing and improving business processes, implanting internal controls, and ensuring the company meets audit and compliance requirements. Complete ad-hoc finance projects, accounting research, and other day-to-day tasks as needed. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Excellent attention to detail and accuracy. Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Proven ability to manage multiple tasks and meet tight deadlines. Strong organizational skills and ability to work independently or collaboratively. Ability to “wear multiple hats” and work in a fast-paced, and cross-functional environment. Demonstrated ability to manage subordinate professionals, build workforce staffing plans, and develop team capability. Strong analytical thinking when evaluating complex accounting transactions, financial results, and reporting issues. Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and department-wide accounting activities. We are looking to add a Principal Accountant, Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting to our team.  If you enjoy working in a startup environment and are passionate about making an impact in a growing company, we would like to hear from you.

In this position, you will be an individual-contributor responsible for owning the Company's internal and external financial reporting, technical accounting, accounting policy, and related compliance activities.

This position serves as the organization's most senior individual-contributor authority on complex U.S. GAAP and SEC reporting matters. The role has principal responsibility for the Company's quarterly and annual financial reporting processes, including preparation and review of Forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K and related disclosures, financial statements, footnotes, MD&A, earnings releases, supporting schedules, and other external reporting requirements.

The role also leads the evaluation and documentation of complex, judgmental, and often first-of-their-kind accounting matters, drives development and maintenance of accounting policy, leads implementation of new accounting standards, advances public-company readiness initiatives, and acts as a senior advisor to management on complicated technical accounting and reporting positions in coordination with external auditors, legal counsel, accounting advisors, and other stakeholders.

The position requires advanced technical accounting judgment, deep SEC reporting expertise, comprehensive knowledge of U.S. GAAP, SOX and internal controls, excellent technical writing and communication skills, and the ability to operate as an internal authority within a complex, fast-paced aerospace/defense environment.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Own and direct the Company's quarterly and annual SEC reporting process, including Forms 10-Q, 10-K, 8-K and other applicable SEC filings, serving as the principal technical authority on filing content.Own the financial reporting calendar and coordinate deliverables across Accounting, FP&A, Legal, Tax, Treasury, Human Resources, Operations, Investor Relations, and other relevant functions.Lead the preparation and review of financial statements, footnotes, MD&A, supporting schedules, selected financial data, and other SEC disclosures.Ensure financial reporting is accurate, complete, timely, and compliant with U.S. GAAP, SEC requirements, Regulation S-X, Regulation S-K, and applicable accounting standards.Serve as the principal evaluator of financial reporting and disclosure implications associated with significant transactions, business developments, strategic initiatives, and changes in the Company's operations.Direct analytical reviews of quarterly and annual financial results and independently resolve significant, unusual, or unexpected fluctuations.Lead the assessment of gaps between the Company's existing financial reporting processes and public-company requirements and drive remediation plans to closure.Establish scalable financial reporting processes, policies, controls, documentation, and governance appropriate for a public-company environment.Own preparation of internal reporting materials for Senior Management and the Board of Directors.Serve as the organization's internal authority and senior advisor on complex U.S. GAAP and SEC accounting matters.Independently research, evaluate, and document accounting conclusions for complex, unusual, non-routine, and highly judgmental transactions.Provide definitive accounting guidance across complex areas including revenue recognition, leases, stock-based compensation, business combinations, debt and equity transactions, impairment, internally developed software, and other complex accounting matters.Monitor new accounting standards, assess their potential impact on the Company, and formulate the Company's position.Lead implementation of new accounting standards and drive development of related accounting policy across the organization.Serve as the principal point of contact for external auditors on financial reporting and technical accounting matters.Direct audit requests and drive timely completion of annual audits and quarterly reviews.Maintain and own documentation supporting significant accounting judgments and estimates.Ad hoc duties as assigned.

Job Requirements And Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.CPA or equivalent advanced certification.Minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in financial reporting and technical accounting, with a strong preference for aerospace, defense, or regulated manufacturing.Extensive experience supporting audits and public-company or IPO-ready environments.Advanced U.S. GAAP knowledge; recognized internal authority on complex technical accounting matters.Advanced knowledge of SEC reporting requirements.Advanced technical writing skills.Extensive experience with FAR/CAS and government contracting accounting.Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel; working knowledge of Word and PowerPoint.Extensive experience with enterprise ERP and reporting systems (e.g., NetSuite, Workiva, OneStream, or equivalent).Advanced audit and internal control expertise.Demonstrated ability to advise senior management on complicated, high-stakes technical accounting positions.Occasional travel between CesiumAstro locations (Austin, TX; Westminster, CO; El Segundo, CA; Melbourne, FL) may be required.Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing, with internal stakeholders, external auditors, and senior leadership.

We are looking to add a Staff Revenue Accountant to our team.  If you enjoy working in a startup environment and are passionate about making an impact in a growing company, we would like to hear from you.

In this position, you will lead revenue recognition and revenue accounting under U.S. GAAP (ASC 606) for CesiumAstro's government and commercial contracts, including Firm Fixed Price, Cost Plus, Time & Materials, and milestone-based arrangements. This role serves as the company's subject matter expert on revenue accounting, partnering with Contracts, Program Management, Business Development, Legal, and FP&A to ensure revenue is recognized accurately and in compliance with applicable accounting standards and government regulations. The Staff Revenue Accountant operates with minimal supervision, exercising a high degree of independent judgment on complex, technical revenue accounting matters.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual revenue accounting close process, ensuring compliance with ASC 606 for all customer contracts.Evaluate new contracts, contract modifications, change orders, and amendments to determine appropriate accounting treatment.Analyze performance obligations, transaction price allocation, variable consideration, and timing of revenue recognition, including over-time recognition using cost-to-cost methodologies where applicable.Prepare and maintain technical accounting memoranda supporting complex revenue conclusions, and review contract assets, contract liabilities, deferred revenue, and unbilled receivables.Partner with Contracts and Program Management to review contract terms prior to award.Support accounting for Firm Fixed Price, Cost Plus, Time & Materials, Cost Reimbursable, IDIQ, Foreign Military Sales, and Direct Commercial Sales contracts.Ensure compliance with applicable FAR, DFARS, and Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), as applicable, and monitor funding modifications, contract options, and change orders for accounting implications.Prepare monthly revenue-related journal entries and reconciliations, and review revenue schedules supporting SEC filings and external financial statements.Support quarterly disclosure requirements related to ASC 606 and coordinate revenue-related audit requests with external auditors.Maintain and enhance SOX-compliant controls over revenue processes, including documentation supporting the quote-to-cash process.Partner with Contracts, Legal, Business Development, Program Management, FP&A, and Controllership to evaluate new contract structures and improve contract language from an accounting perspective.Support proposal development and optimize revenue recognition outcomes for new business opportunities.Identify and drive opportunities for continuous process improvement within revenue accounting workflows.

Job Requirements And Minimum Qualifications

8 years of progressive revenue accounting experience with a B.S./B.A. in Accounting or Finance required or a minimum of 6 years of experience with a relevant M.S./M.A.CPA required.Advanced expertise in ASC 606 Revenue Recognition and ASC 340 Contract Costs.Extensive experience with government contract structures, contract modifications, and variable consideration.Strong knowledge of Stand-alone Selling Price (SSP), Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO), contract assets/liabilities, deferred revenue, and unbilled receivables.Working knowledge of internal controls over financial reporting and financial statement presentation.Experience with government contracting regulations (FAR/DFARS), project accounting, and percentage-of-completion accounting.SOX compliance and technical accounting research experience required.Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills to resolve complex revenue accounting matters.Clear verbal and written communication skills.Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.Experience with ERP systems such as Oracle, SAP, NetSuite, Acumatica, or Microsoft Dynamics.Experience with revenue automation and revenue management tools.Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

Preferred Experience

Experience with defense or aerospace manufacturing and public company reporting.

We are looking to add a Staff Cost Accountant to our team.  If you enjoy working in a startup environment and are passionate about making an impact in a growing company, we would like to hear from you.

In this role you will lead cost accounting, standard costing, and manufacturing accounting for CesiumAstro's aerospace and defense manufacturing operations. This role owns inventory valuation and cost accounting processes and partners with Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Engineering, and FP&A to improve financial performance, serving as an individual contributor and the company's subject matter expert on cost accounting matters. The Staff Cost Accountant operates with minimal supervision, exercising a high degree of independent judgment on complex, technical accounting matters.

Job Duties And Responsibilities

Lead the monthly close process for all cost accounting activities, including review and approval of inventory-related journal entries.Own and maintain the standard costing system, ensuring accurate product costing across the business.Lead annual and interim cost updates, including development of labor and overhead rates.Partner with Engineering and Operations to validate manufacturing standards, analyze bill of material (BOM) and routing changes, and evaluate cost impacts of engineering changes and new product introductions.Oversee accounting for material consumption, labor capitalization, manufacturing overhead, production variances, scrap, rework, yield losses, and inventory adjustments.Ensure manufacturing transactions and production order close processes are recorded accurately and timely.Oversee perpetual inventory accounting, physical inventory observations, and cycle count programs, investigating discrepancies as needed.Review excess and obsolete inventory reserves and evaluate lower-of-cost-or-net-realizable-value (LCNRV) considerations.Prepare and review monthly variance analyses, including purchase price, material usage, labor, overhead, efficiency, scrap/yield, and production volume variances.Communicate operational drivers of variances and recommend corrective actions to Operations and finance leadership.Prepare inventory and cost accounting schedules supporting monthly financial statements, including account reconciliations for inventory, cost of sales, manufacturing variances, and inventory reserves.Support SEC reporting requirements related to inventory and cost of sales and support external audit requests.Maintain SOX-compliant controls over inventory and cost accounting and support internal and external SOX testing.Serve as the primary accounting business partner for Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Procurement, Engineering, Production Planning, Program Management, Quality, and FP&A.Identify and drive opportunities for continuous process improvement and automation within cost accounting workflows.

Job Requirements And Minimum Qualifications

Minimum of 8 years of progressive cost accounting or manufacturing accounting experience with a B.S./B.A. in Accounting or a minimum of 6 years of experience with a relevant M.S./M.A.CPA or CMA required.Advanced expertise in U.S. GAAP inventory accounting, including ASC 330 – Inventory.Extensive experience with standard costing, actual costing, and manufacturing overhead allocation.Strong knowledge of cost rollups, BOM management, routing structures, and standard cost revisions.Advanced knowledge of inventory reserves, obsolescence analysis, physical inventory controls, and cycle counts.Strong understanding of inventory capitalization, capitalized manufacturing costs, and fixed asset capitalization for manufacturing equipment.Working knowledge of SOX internal controls and ERP manufacturing modules.Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.Experience with ERP systems such as Acumatica, Oracle, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, or NetSuite.Proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications, including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive.Experience with FactoryLogix or similar manufacturing execution systems (MES).Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills to resolve complex cost accounting and manufacturing issues.

Preferred Experience

Experience with defense or aerospace manufacturing, government contracting, and public company reporting.
